Duties are but not limited to: The ANM demonstrates leadership, experience, and creative approaches in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others.

The ANM, in collaboration with the Education Department, develops, coordinates, and provides ongoing education to nursing personnel for knowledge and skills enhancement while ensuring clinical competence.

The ANM may cover in the absence of the Nurse Manager and represents the Nurse Executive during non-administrative hours .The ANM RN is a professional RN qualified by education and experience to provide professional leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others.

Provides professional psychiatric and/or medical nursing care to acute and chronically ill Veterans. The ANM is accountable for adhering to established policies and standards of care and practice.

The ANM is responsible for assisting the NM in supervision and administration of nursing care delivery, managing nursing personnel, and coordinating all related activities. The ANM demonstrates leadership in developing and implementing programs to improve the delivery of patient care. Will maintain clinical proficiency in area of oversight.

The ANM will evaluate procedural, pharmacological, and other therapeutic treatment regimen, monitoring to ensure compliance with all medical center policies and procedures.

Will successfully transition new hires into the position by promptly communicating performance elements and standards within applicable timeframes, providing ongoing feedback and coaching, and making appropriate use of the probationary period to assess the employee's ability to perform.

Preferred Experience: - Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) preferred; advanced nursing or leadership education is highly desirable. - Minimum of 2 or 3 years of recent nursing experience in an acute inpatient psychiatric/mental health setting preferred. - Previous charge nurse, team lead, supervisory, or nursing leadership experience preferred. - Experience caring for patients with acute psychiatric conditions, behavioral emergencies, suicide/self-harm risk, aggression, and complex behavioral needs. - Demonstrated experience with de-escalation, crisis intervention, restraint/seclusion reduction, and maintaining a safe therapeutic environment. - Knowledge of levels of observation, environmental and ligature-risk safety, contraband/hazardous-item management, and inpatient psychiatric safety practices. - Experience with staff supervision, scheduling, performance management, coaching, education, and competency development. - Experience supporting quality improvement, regulatory compliance, patient safety, and survey readiness. - Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with psychiatry, social work, psychology, nursing, VA Police, and other interdisciplinary team members. - Strong communication, conflict-resolution, clinical judgment, and leadership skills in a high-acuity environment.

VALLHCS is an interdisciplinary facility serving medical, surgical, behavioral health, inpatient, outpatients, and residential treatment. This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity.

This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing. Transferring patients and objects may be required.

The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations or operative/invasive procedures. The incumbent will be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on Veteran needs.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Manages the administration and evaluation of nursing care, program implementation, personnel management, and overall operations for the Dialysis Unit, home dialysis program, and acute dialysis in the ICU units.

Manages delivery of quality patient care, including appropriate documentation, employee clinical/performance competency, and continuous National and VAPAHCS performance-improvement measures consistent with the VAPAHCS mission. Oversees and monitors employee adherence to VHA Privacy/HIPAA and Information Security rules and regulations.

Directly coordinates staffing, physical facilities, supplies, and equipment for nursing services provided to patients 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Leads retention and recruitment of highly skilled nursing staff; monitors workflow, technical, and equipment needs; and ensures the workforce can adapt to a rapidly changing environment.

Ensures employees complete mandatory annual, facility, and nursing training and reviews within required time frames. Ensures annual appraisals/proficiencies are completed, communicated to employees, and submitted timely.

Maintains familiarity with established policies and procedures; administers the unit in accordance with The Joint Commission (TJC) and VHA policy; and ensures staff compliance with VAPAHCS and unit-based policies and procedures.

Applies and completes reports related to policy and procedures, including staffing reconciliation, payroll exceptions, risk management, patient incidents, personnel accidents, EEO, and sexual-harassment allegations.

Participates in designing, implementing, monitoring, and revising systems that promote cost-effective resource use, effective staffing, and enhanced patient care using System Redesign principles.

Provides leadership and collaborates with the interdisciplinary team to improve and sustain service quality and effectiveness; applies professional practice and TJC standards to program development, analysis, and management; and promotes evidence-based practice for optimal patient outcomes.

Collaborates with the Nursing Perioperative Management Team to identify and promote staff development, strengthen staff competencies, and advance System Redesign initiatives; works with the Chief Nurse of Nursing Perioperative on program development, quality care, performance measures, and resource planning.

Maintains an integrated delivery system through expansion of clinical practices. Maintains operational efficiencies through emphasis on safe practices and National Safety. Actively implements Lean principles, supports quality-improvement projects, and promotes a culture of continuous quality improvement.

Supports excellence in research, training, and education through ongoing competency. Performs other duties as assigned.

Develops/reviews nursing functional statements, position descriptions, competencies, performance appraisals, and performance plans.

Utilizes organization, critical thinking, leadership and problem-solving skills to address/identify/resolve nursing administrative and clinical issues.

Ensures administrative and clinical applications reflect VA standards of patient education, treatment interventions, outcome re-evaluations, and adherence to Nursing Service and VA Healthcare policies, including all new VA directives.

Gathers data from personal observation to assist in ongoing improvement/customization of training for Nursing Senior Leadership and staff. Demonstrates expert knowledge and ability to apply principles of evidence-based practice, monitors and reports effectiveness of change outcomes to Nursing Senior Leadership.

The primary function of the CCICM RN is provide coordination and direct clinical evidence-based services including, assessments and interventions; program development; Veteran, family, caregiver and staff education on Care Coordination and Integrated Case Management (CCICM); resource development; community outreach; continuous quality improvement activities, and evaluation/consultation.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Serves as a CCICM subject matter expert. Participates in the development of policies, procedures, and practice guidelines for the program and participates in facility, VISN, and national program development as related to CCICM.

Ensures compliance with VHA Directive 1110.04, Integrated Case Management Standards of Practice. Provides guidance and support in the implementation and maintenance of the program through education, training, mentorship, and coaching. Participates in the development of, and implements policies and procedures specific to the Aleda E.

Lutz VA Medical Center and ensures compliance with local facility, VISN, Patient Experience Initiatives, VA Central Office (VACO) directives and handbooks, as well as Joint Commission, and other accrediting bodies and regulatory standards as needed.

Ensures full collaboration with social work counterpart, for all planning, development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the CCICM operations. Manages, monitors, evaluates and reports on all CCICM related data to fully capture the day-to-day functioning and practice impacts on the facility and Veteran care.

Plans, organizes, and directs CCICM operations, in conjunction with the CCICM Executive Sponsor, social work counterpart(s) and the ADPCS. Identifies Veteran cohorts across the Aleda E. Lutz VA Medical Center with the highest opportunity and highest need.

Including development and implementation of a monitoring process for ongoing screening and identified cohort(s). Identifies and tracks potential areas where care coordination is taking place to include but not limited to primary care, surgical care, mental health, community care, specialty clinics, geriatrics, chronic disease, and homeless programs.

Ensures integration with the facility level care coordination and case management teams to include but not limited to Nurses and Social Workers, care coordinators, care managers, and case managers of, both inpatient and outpatient for seamless continuity of care.

Develops, implements and tracks facility wide CCICM education plan to key stakeholders to include Service Chiefs, supervisors/managers, frontline staff, and Veterans with plan for ongoing sustainment. Develops, implement, and monitor processes for ongoing screening and identified cohort. ?

Actively participates in the treatment planning process with other disciplines, including involvement in discharge planning with other disciplines and will be responsible for ensuring that discharge plans are executed in a manner that are timely and appropriate.

Actively participates in unit quality improvement processes and initiatives, as well as Veteran experience/customer service programs and initiatives. Develops, maintains effective working relationships with key medical center staff and community agencies to enhance the scope and functioning of Veterans assigned.

Ability to develop needed community support and/or resources to ensure the program goals are achieved. Provides guidance, education, and direction to the Care Coordination Review Team (CCRT).

Ensuring full participation by setting expectations, clear roles, and responsibilities when assigning a Lead Coordinator to Veterans identified as needing moderate or complex care coordination services.

Provides direct patient care services to identified high utilizer/at-risk Veterans to ensure appropriate services are in place to support the CCICM framework. Preferred: Candidates in possession of and provide proof of BLS Certification will be considered best qualified.

Major Duties include, but are not limited to: Provide direct nursing care and case management for Veterans with chronic and complex pain conditions within the primary care setting.

Collaborate with physicians, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, psychologists, and other interdisciplinary team members to develop and implement individualized pain management care plans. Conduct comprehensive pain assessments and monitor treatment efficacy and side effects.

Support safe opioid prescribing practices, including monitoring compliance with Opioid Safety Initiative (OSI) guidelines, informed consent processes, and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) checks.

Educate Veterans and caregivers on pain management options, including non-pharmacological modalities (e.g., Whole Health, mindfulness, physical therapy referrals, acupuncture) and safe medication use.

Coordinate referrals to specialty pain clinics, behavioral health, physical medicine and rehabilitation, and complementary/integrative health services. Monitor high-risk patients for signs of substance use disorder, diversion, or adverse outcomes, and escalate concerns per protocol.

Document care thoroughly and accurately in the electronic health record (CPRS/Cerner) in compliance with VA and Joint Commission standards. The Outpatient Mental Health RN assumes the following major duties and responsibilities: 1) Is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising patient care. 2) Utilizes designated templates for CPRS for assigned department, and completes nursing notes in alignment with ANA Guidelines, Nursing Policy, and Nurse Competency training. 3) Serves as a liaison for warm handoffs, as needed for psychiatric concerns and initiates referrals between mental health clinics for urgent mental health needs including potential evaluation for acute Inpatient Mental health care. 4) Completes Clinical Reminders when due, and actively collaborates with treating/covering provider on required follow-up. 5) Manages secure messages for designated Providers. 6) Follows continuum of care agreements within Mental Health service and across services. 7) If indicated facilitates Measurement-Based Care (MBC) in person, by telephone and discusses finding in the development of the treatment plan with the patient and treatment team. 8) Completes a Suicide risk assessment which each mental health encounter when the patient has not already been evaluated by another clinician in the same day.

Applies additional interventions in alignment with policy, and actively communicates with their team to mitigate risk and provide needed follow-up. 9) Completes a Columbia Suicide Severity Risk Screening (CSSRS) when due or indicated & applies additional interventions in alignment with VHA Policy. 10) Completes a Suicide Behavior Overdose Reports [SBOR] when the patient reports a behavior that is not already documented and that could increase the risk for suicide such as but not limited to attempted suicide or preparatory behaviors (hoarding medication or purchasing a lethal weapon with the intent to harm self).

Communicates risk with Provider and Suicide Prevention Counselor (SPC). 11) Completes a Suicide Safety Plan in alignment with policy and in the development of the treatment plan. 12) Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient transition through the continuum of care, patient and family education, patient self management after discharge, and supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction. 13) Considers all characteristics of the individual, including age and life stages, state of health, race and culture, values, and previous experiences. 14) Demonstrates effective interpersonal skills and therapeutic interventions with patients. 15) Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. 16) Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. 17) Core elements of performance include knowledge and active participation in unit/program level quality improvement processes and initiatives as well as customer service programs. 18) Conducts chart audits and takes remedial actions as designated by the Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manger, Section Chief, or Associate Nurse Executive for Mental Health. 19) Completes Safe Patient Handling and Mobility training on hire and as designated by Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager, and Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health. 20) Maintains appropriate level of PMDB per Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager and Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health. 21) Other duties as designed by the IMPACT Unit per Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager, Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health, Section Chief.

Die Akutstation S2 wendet sich an Menschen in psychiatrischen Ausnahmesituationen, welche auf sofortige Hilfe angewiesen sind. Diesen Menschen bieten wir professionelle Unterstützung. Wir leisten Hilfe in der akuten Phase.

Dazu gehört eine psychiatrische Notfallversorgung mit einer sorgfältigen Diagnostik, entsprechender Behandlung sowie einer zügigen Abklärung der sozialen Situation. Ziele der Behandlung sind der Wiederaufbau von Alltagsfertigkeiten, die Erarbeitung möglicher Bewältigungsstrategien und die Stabilisierung des Selbstwertgefühls.

Entsprechend dem Behandlungsschwerpunkt bietet die Station diverse spezifische Therapien und Interventionen an (z.B. Stimmeninterview, IPT, etc.). Im Rahmen des Modell Recovery ist zudem ein Peer\-Mitarbeiter fester Bestandteil des Behandlungsteams. Die Station ist in der Regel offen geführt und implementiert das Safewards\-Modell.

Lebensjahr, umfassend behandelt und begleitet. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Diagnostik, Therapie und Prävention psychischer Erkrankungen, die im Zusammenhang mit dem Alter auftreten oder durch altersbedingte Veränderungen begünstigt werden können.
Mit fachlicher Kompetenz, Einfühlungsvermögen und einem ganzheitlichen Blick begleiten Sie unsere Patientinnen und Patienten durch ihren individuellen Pflege\- und Behandlungsprozess. Dabei übernehmen Sie Verantwortung für die professionelle Steuerung der Pflege und arbeiten eng mit dem interprofessionellen Behandlungsteam sowie Angehörigen und externen Partnern zusammen.
Ihr Aufgabengebiet
Bezugspersonenarbeit und pflegerische Fallführung: Sie planen, steuern und evaluieren den Pflegeprozess der Ihnen zugeteilten Patientinnen und Patienten.
Schichtverantwortung: Sie koordinieren die Schicht fachlich, setzen Prioritäten und sorgen für eine klare Aufgabenverteilung und Delegation innerhalb des Pflegeteams.
Psychiatrische Pflege: Sie beurteilen den psychischen Zustand, erkennen Veränderungen frühzeitig und handeln bei Krisen und herausfordernden Situationen professionell und situationsgerecht.
Alterspsychiatrische Pflege: Sie begleiten Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Krankheitsbildern wie Demenz, Delir, Depression, Abhängigkeitserkrankungen oder Psychosen sowie bei psychiatrischer und somatischer Multimorbidität.
Angehörigenarbeit: Sie beraten und begleiten Angehörige und beziehen diese angemessen in den Behandlungsprozess ein.
Interprofessionelle Zusammenarbeit: Sie bringen Ihre pflegerische Expertise in Visiten und Fallbesprechungen ein und wirken aktiv bei der Festlegung und Überprüfung der Behandlungsziele mit.
Austritts\- und Übergangsmanagement: Sie gestalten gemeinsam mit dem Behandlungsteam tragfähige Anschlusslösungen und arbeiten dabei mit Spitex, Heimen, Zuweisenden und weiteren externen Partnern zusammen.
Dabei schaffen Sie eine vertrauensvolle und wertschätzende Atmosphäre, in der sich unsere Patientinnen und Patienten sicher, genommen und professionell begleitet fühlen.

About RPM

Roman Pennsylvania Medical, P.C. (RPM) is a telehealth practice dedicated to providing high-quality, patient-centric care. RPM is part of the provider network affiliated with Ro, a direct-to-patient healthcare company. Providers help patients seeking care through Ro’s platform for their mental health, women’s health, men’s health, fertility, metabolic health, and skincare needs.

RPM providers benefit from using technology, tools, and solutions designed to support safe and appropriate care, reduce administrative burden, and help them seamlessly connect with patients throughout their care journeys. As part of RPM’s affiliation with Ro, providers help expand access to affordable, high-quality care to more patients.

RPM’s nationwide network of providers is made up of board-certified physicians, nurse practitioners, and nurses licensed to treat patients in all 50 states and Washington, DC.

As a 6-month contracted Virtual Registered Nurse, you’ll partner with RPM Providers and work independently to provide high-quality patient care through EMR messaging and communications, and triage to ensure safety, productivity, and team optimization are maintained at the practice level.

You are passionate about working in non-traditional healthcare settings and expanding patient access. You can troubleshoot challenging situations as they arise and ensure high-quality patient care is provided per RPM principles and guidelines. You will report to an RN Lead throughout the length of your contract.

Who are you? That's a great question. You are a Virtual Registered Nurse who refuses to settle for the status quo. You apply your nursing knowledge and your desire to help people live happier, more productive lives to your daily work.

You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, you are highly technologically savvy, and you are a problem solver who enjoys working collaboratively with others. We don’t expect you to know everything about medicine or telemedicine, but we do expect you to be ready to dive in and learn.

Provide comprehensive clinical care by independently managing direct patient needs, including message triage, counseling, and education to patients in our sexual health and metabolic health care verticals.
Complete tasks such as side effect management, efficacy counseling, and overall clinical practice support.

Review lab results using approved protocols to provide targeted lifestyle coaching and patient education for weight management.
Serve as a resource for the non-clinical Care Team, addressing day-to-day clinical questions and concerns.

Duties and responsibilities of the AMBULATORY SURGERY REGISTERED NURSE include, but are not limited to: Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse (RN), provides preoperative/ procedural care, including (but not limited to) the nursing assessment of patients, consent, and H&P validations, the starting of intravenous fluids including venipuncture, assisting with peripheral nerve blocks, assuring all lab work and other pre-operative/procedural testing is completed and communicated to team members, confirms surgical sites are prepared and marked, and the administration of medications as ordered.

Provides clear and concise preoperative teaching and reviews discharge instructions to patients and families with written and verbal communication. The Ambulatory RN monitors post-operative patient's level of consciousness after the recovery of anesthesia/sedation. Closely observes signs of side effect of post residual anesthesia medications.

The Ambulatory RN maintains knowledge of current American Society of Peri Anesthesia Nurses (ASPAN) standards, VHA Directive, and service level standard operating procedures. The Ambulatory RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documentation of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record.

Responsible for participating within unit based and/or organizational level Shared Governance councils, utilizing clinical expertise, evidence-based practice, and knowledge to assist with finding solutions to problems or issues to improve the quality care provided to our veterans.

The staff nurse working on a Mental Health Residential Rehabilitation Domiciliary is a professional nurse with a broad based clinical knowledge enabling him/her to effectively implement health promotion, prevention and recovery-based programming for adult residents throughout the residential continuum of care.

The Residential staff nurse functions as a part of an interdisciplinary team in partnership with the Mental Health Treatment Team, Veterans, and families promoting wellness through effective holistic, recovery-oriented treatment, and the management of mental health disorders including substance abuse, PTSD, traumatic brain injury, and serious mental illness.

The Registered Nurse creates and maintains a safe, therapeutic, recovery-oriented environment in collaboration with Veterans and other healthcare providers. (VHA Directive 1162.02) The staff nurse utilizes the nursing process when assessing, planning, implementing, evaluating, and documenting nursing care provided.

The Registered Nurse in the Minimum Data Set (MDS) program is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, coordinating, and evaluating patient care across the continuum of care.

The nurse promotes patient education, self-management, safety, and customer satisfaction while collaborating with the interdisciplinary healthcare team to improve patient outcomes.

As nurses progress from Nurse I to Nurse III, they demonstrate increasing levels of clinical expertise, leadership, independent decision-making, mentoring, quality improvement, and program-level responsibility.

The position requires knowledge of long-term care standards, evidence-based practice, management of acute and chronic illnesses, and palliative and hospice care, while ensuring compliance with Veterans Health Administration, CMS, and Joint Commission requirements.

Key Duties and Responsibilities Assess, plan, implement, coordinate, and evaluate individualized patient care. Administer medications, treatments, and procedures according to established policies and guidelines. Coordinate care, patient education, and self-management activities to support positive health outcomes.

Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure safe, effective, and patient-centered care. Apply evidence-based practice and participate in quality improvement and performance improvement initiatives. Advocate for patient safety, rights, satisfaction, and ethical nursing practice.

Support professional development through continuing education, mentoring, and knowledge sharing. Lead and contribute to program, unit, or service-level initiatives that improve patient care outcomes and nursing practice. Maintain compliance with VA policies, long-term care regulations, CMS requirements, and Joint Commission standards.

Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, leadership, and continuous improvement in patient care delivery.

The Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) practices in Mental Health (MH) Service to provide a full range of services emphasizing quality, timeliness, and the advancement of the Veterans Affairs (VA) mission. The PMHNP provides advanced clinical practice, consultation, and management.

The PMHNP practices to the full extent of their education, training, and certification. Core functions are outlined in the clinical privileges that correspond with this position. The PMHNP has prescriptive authority as indicated by their position.

FUNCTIONS OF ASSIGNED DUTIES: The PMHNP is a licensed independent practitioner with advanced education and national certification who provides evidence-based care for a population of patients.

Major duties and responsibilities of the position: Uses advanced clinical judgment to independently provide evidence-based treatment to Veterans with acute or chronic mental illness including use of psychotropic medications, psychotherapy, and other modalities.

Provides patient and family education on medical/MH conditions, preventive measures, and prescribed treatments. Demonstrates leadership and engages in collaboration with other MH and specialty care professionals while involving Veterans and their families (as appropriate), in treatment plan development.

Assesses and adjusts the plan of care as needed to achieve optimal patient outcomes. Counsels and treats patients with substance use disorders. Orders and interprets labs, tests, and diagnostic studies. Initiates referrals and consults to specialty services.

Exemplifies the ICARE core values of-Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence.
